This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via admin_rescue (literal, a string literal in checkExcludeSubmitterPolicyPairing), auto_approve (literal, a string literal in a comment in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema; a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in checkExcludeSubmitterPolicyPairing), onEmptyApprovers (literal, a string literal in checkExcludeSubmitterPolicyPairing))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via auto_approve (literal, a string literal in a comment in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema; a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in checkExcludeSubmitterPolicyPairing))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via admin_rescue (literal, a string literal in checkExcludeSubmitterPolicyPairing), auto_approve (literal, a string literal in a comment in ApprovalNodeConfigSchema; a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in checkExcludeSubmitterPolicyPairing), onEmptyApprovers (literal, a string literal in checkExcludeSubmitterPolicyPairing))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b77bb37eb2c738c40093acb04f19fa8fc2dd605a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1aad63f8d0623425884ca79a4ee1c8306e4ed4cf` — the merge of head `3cee74ecf009d339aaf97ba19c83c061df7e0414` into base `b77bb37eb2c738c40093acb04f19fa8fc2dd605a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1aad63f8d0623425884ca79a4ee1c8306e4ed4cf && git checkout 1aad63f8d0623425884ca79a4ee1c8306e4ed4cf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b77bb37eb2c738c40093acb04f19fa8fc2dd605a 3cee74ecf009d339aaf97ba19c83c061df7e0414 && git checkout -B drift-repro b77bb37eb2c738c40093acb04f19fa8fc2dd605a && git merge --no-ff 3cee74ecf009d339aaf97ba19c83c061df7e0414

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b77bb37eb2c738c40093acb04f19fa8fc2dd605a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b77bb37eb2c738c40093acb04f19fa8fc2dd605a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #25635 · `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT` · 2026-10-24T18:31Z · head `3cee74ecf0` · report `6387948614` (on #25635; os-dev subagent of this session) · seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. The path limb hits (`packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts`), and the change is a narrowing, so a same-shape `## Contract review` PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the landing head is owed. `needs:contract-review` is added in this stroke. **Release window:** this must merge before the next objectstack release, so the review is asked for first.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #25635`. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and `Ruling-ref: 6386627950` are line-initial in the body and the changeset (`@objectstack/spec` `minor`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reasons). 4 files, +172/−7: `approval.zod.ts`, its test file, the regenerated `references/automation/approval.mdx` row, and the changeset. Not governed. `origin/main` merged once through `os-regen-merge.sh`, clean.
2. **The ruling, measured on the diff.** Letter A: `checkExcludeSubmitterPolicyPairing` is a second `.superRefine` on `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema`, chained after `checkFallbackApproversPairing`, in its shape. It raises one `custom` issue at `onEmptyApprovers` only when `excludeSubmitter === true` and `onEmptyApprovers === 'auto_approve'`. The message names both keys and prescribes `admin_rescue` / `fail` / `fallback` with `fallbackApprovers`. It deliberately does not offer dropping `excludeSubmitter`, which would drop the control. `false` or an omitted key leaves `auto_approve` its meaning. The `excludeSubmitter` describe gains one sentence naming the refused value; the `[PLANNED]` marker stays.
3. **Changeset, checked line by line.**
   - "Narrows nothing a released version accepted": the report's reading of the npm `@objectstack/spec` 18.1.0 tarball, 0 files with `excludeSubmitter` (controls `onEmptyApprovers` 28, `fallbackApprovers` 30), and the key's own changeset still pending.
   - "Only `true` arms it" and "every other policy parses": the guard's two strict equalities.
   - "The approval engine is unchanged": no `plugin-approvals` file in the diff.
4. **Gates.** Check-runs on `3cee74ecf0` at this record: 39; 22 completed with none failed, 17 still running. Local, per the report:
   - 113/113 derived, `--ran` DERIVED zero. Four needed a re-run (three during a concurrent `dist` rebuild, one lock timeout); all exited 0.
   - spec 719 files / 21800 tests. Consumers in full: `plugin-approvals` 96 / 1259, `lint` 161 / 7269, `metadata-protocol` 263 / 21475.
   - spec `test:repo` 79 / 1269, before the merge. The dogfood battery is 295 files, green.
   - TDD red: 6 failed before the implementation. Ablation on the `.superRefine` anchor: 5 red, restored blob-identical.
   - Landing waits for every check green and the contract-review PASS.
5. **Deviations and the open question.**
   - (a) `test:repo` was run once, before the merge; CI Test Core owns the post-merge run. The named consumers declare no `test:repo`. Accepted.
   - (b) The declaration arm: the dev asks whether `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` should stay, though no *published* accept set narrows. **Stays (A):** the claim set it, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` already makes the gate classify the change identically, and the changeset says in words that nothing published narrows. The contract review may say otherwise.
   - `mcp_calls` 0; relay writes 2.
6. **Out-of-scope outcomes.** Two existing prescriptions still list `'auto_approve'` among the policies to choose: the lint hint of `approval-expression-no-empty-policy` (`validate-approval-approvers.ts` about `:625`, the dev's finding), and, in the seat's own reading, `checkFallbackApproversPairing`'s message (`approval.zod.ts` about `:814`). An author with `excludeSubmitter: true` who follows either is refused at once by the new arm, with its prescription. That is loud, not silent, and no producer writes `excludeSubmitter`: Acceptance notes, no carrier. SLA `escalation.action: 'auto_approve'` is a different key, outside the ruling.
7. **Landing.** Not governed, 179 changed lines. Once a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS is on record and every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3cee74ecf009d339aaf97ba19c83c061df7e0414`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts` + `packages/spec/src/automation/approval-exclude-submitter-25609.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts` (prose faces `.changeset/25635-exclude-submitter-auto-approve.md`, `content/docs/references/automation/approval.mdx` read, not scope)

### ① Derived judgments

- **Declaration is right.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: an approval node config that previously parsed (`excludeSubmitter: true` with `onEmptyApprovers: 'auto_approve'`) is now refused at the parse. That is a served-set narrowing of a metadata-protocol key, so both lines are owed and both are present. `Ruling-ref: 6386627950` matches batch #12 item 1 letter A (maintainer 「25635  25647  25675 同意」).
- **Implementation matches the ruling letter.** `checkExcludeSubmitterPolicyPairing` raises exactly one `custom` issue when `excludeSubmitter === true && onEmptyApprovers === 'auto_approve'` and nothing otherwise; it is chained as a second `.superRefine` after `checkFallbackApproversPairing`, so the two pairings are independent (pinned in §6). `false` / absent `excludeSubmitter` keeps `auto_approve` legal; every other policy still parses beside `true`. The ruling asked for 「多一条配对校验（形如 checkFallbackApproversPairing），提示改用 admin_rescue / fail / fallback」: the message names both keys and offers exactly those three policies.
- **Issue placement on `onEmptyApprovers` is accepted.** The ruled fix is to change the policy, so that is the key the author edits. The PR's reason for not offering "remove excludeSubmitter" as an equal fix is sound (the cheaper edit drops the control the author asked for).
- **Doors carry the refusal in the contract's own words.** `FlowSchema` reports it at `nodes.N.config.onEmptyApprovers`; the build judge `flowNodeConfigRefusals` reports `node-config-refused-by-contract` on the same key. Both pinned. No door-side rewording, no second copy of the rule.
- **Describe/TSDoc now say what the code enforces.** The `excludeSubmitter` describe gains the refused value and the three alternatives; `[PLANNED — not yet enforced]` stays, which is correct because the runtime exclusion (#25573) is still open. `approval.mdx` is the regenerated row only.
- **No published surface narrows.** The PR's release-window reading (18.1.0 tarball: 0 hits for `excludeSubmitter`; CHANGELOG 0 hits; the key's own changeset `.changeset/25609-approval-exclude-submitter.md` still pending) is consistent with the card and ruling history: #25609 landed after 18.1.0 (2026-10-24 09:18Z). So the refusal and the key ship in the same release. ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is justified on those facts.
- **Window.** This must merge before the next objectstack release. If a release cuts first, the changeset needs a fresh ADR-0087 disposition and the declaration stays `narrowed` but the `no-migration-prescription` reading no longer holds. Spec seat: land it ahead of the next release train.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/spec': minor` is correct: `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` takes at least `minor` (AGENTS.md step 3), and nothing here reaches `major`. Title carries `!` and the changeset carries the three declaration lines. All 47 check runs on head `3cee74ecf0` are `success` or `skipped` (Test Core 1–6/6, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Type Check ×5, Lint ×9, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, claim gates); none red, none pending.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Lint hint `approval-expression-no-empty-policy`** still lists `'auto_approve'` among the policies to declare regardless of `excludeSubmitter`. Following it verbatim beside `excludeSubmitter: true` is refused at once by this rule with the prescription, so it is loud, not silent. Noted, no carrier; the `checkFallbackApproversPairing` message likewise still names `'auto_approve'` and is covered the same way.
- **SLA `escalation.action: 'auto_approve'`** is a different, timed key outside ruling 6386627950. Untouched; correctly out of scope.
- **Runtime exclusion (#25573)** remains the second half of #25609; this PR does not pretend to it.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-25635-exclude-submitter-auto-approve-refusal`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bf4vhia9fHNXpqC1PCfxie`

**VERDICT: PASS**
